First pre-release of **Gurkha Launcher**, a Minecraft: Java Edition launcher for Android based on [Zalith Launcher](https://github.com/ZalithLauncher/ZalithLauncher) and [PojavLauncher](https://github.com/PojavLauncherTeam/PojavLauncher).

### Which file should I download?

- **Most phones (64-bit ARM):** `GurkhaLauncher-1.0.0-beta.5-arm64-v8a.apk`
- **Older or low-end 32-bit phones:** `GurkhaLauncher-1.0.0-beta.5-armeabi-v7a.apk`
- **x86 tablets, Chromebooks and emulators:** `GurkhaLauncher-1.0.0-beta.5-x86_64.apk` (or `-x86.apk`)
- **Not sure:** `GurkhaLauncher-1.0.0-beta.5.apk` (works everywhere, larger download)

Gurkha Launcher installs as its own app (`com.gurkha.launcher`) next to Zalith Launcher, with its own settings and game files.

### Changes compared to Zalith Launcher

- New logo: two crossed khukuris (launcher icon, themed icon on Android 13+, notification icon).

**Minecraft 26.1 and newer:**
- Minecraft 26.3 replaced GLFW with SDL3 (LWJGL 3.4.1), which made it crash on Zalith-based launchers. Gurkha Launcher now ships LWJGL 3.4.1 and SDL3 for these versions and lets SDL run on the game surface (ported from Amethyst).
- Minecraft 26.2 crashed at startup: it needs LWJGL's Vulkan, VMA, SPIRV-Cross and shaderc libraries, which the launcher's older LWJGL didn't have. 26.1 and 26.2 now run on LWJGL 3.4.1, the version they are made for. Typing in a text field no longer crashes 26.1+ (a missing keyboard function), and 26.2's monitor setup no longer fails. Checked by resolving every LWJGL class, method and field that Minecraft 1.21.11, 26.1.2, 26.2, 26.3 and 26.4 Snapshot 4 use against the libraries the launcher gives them: nothing is missing.
- Minecraft 26.2+ can render with Vulkan, and since the 26.4 snapshots its "Default" setting means Vulkan, without going back to OpenGL after a crash. The launcher's renderers are OpenGL renderers, so "Default" now starts these versions with OpenGL. To try Vulkan, choose it under **Video Settings > Graphics API**.
- Quitting 26.2+ no longer leaves a frozen game screen (and a running game notification) behind.
- New **LTW** renderer (OpenGL 3/4 on top of OpenGL ES 3, latest build of MojoLauncher's LTW). Minecraft 1.21.5 and newer, and Sodium on 1.17+, are switched to LTW automatically, since GL4ES can't run them; versions before 1.17 keep using GL4ES. On Adreno GPUs, versions before 1.21.5 without Sodium are limited to 7 chunks of render distance (a driver limit).
- 26.3+ needs a device with OpenGL ES 3 (for LTW).

**32-bit devices (armeabi-v7a):**
- Fixed the game crashing on 32-bit devices when its window size changes (for example right after start, when the navigation bar hides, or when the keyboard opens): the window handle was passed to Java as a 32-bit value instead of a 64-bit one (ported from PojavLauncher).
- Java 17, 21 and 25 now run in client VM mode on 32-bit ARM (C1 compiler, Serial GC, small code cache), like PojavLauncher's own 32-bit Java builds, which its developers found to be more stable.
- Fixed Minecraft 1.20.5+ crashing or rendering garbage on 32-bit ARM: Java 21 and 25 returned wrong results for `Math.abs/sqrt/sin/cos/tan/log/exp/pow` there, and Java's own `StrictMath` then failed with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. These math shortcuts are now turned off on 32-bit ARM (PojavLauncher's fix, checked on the bundled Java 17, 21 and 25 under 32-bit ARM emulation).
- The 32-bit "free address space" warning no longer holds the launch; its estimate is written to the game log instead.

**CurseForge:**
- Mods and modpacks list all their versions. Before, only the newest 50 files of a project were shown (the launcher asked CurseForge for 500 at a time, more than it allows), so older Minecraft versions of popular mods were missing.
- Modpacks start downloading much sooner: the download links and checksums of all mods come in one request per 100 mods instead of two or three requests per mod.
- Files without a download link from CurseForge use their CDN link instead of being skipped, and unusual projects no longer break a whole search.
- CurseForge needs an API key built into the app. Without one, the CurseForge pages now say so instead of showing "no results", and the download pages start on Modrinth.

**Smaller download:**
- The APKs are 19 to 45 MB smaller than the builds before: 64-bit ARM 166 → 148 MB, 32-bit ARM 159 → 140 MB, x86_64 172 → 147 MB, x86 145 → 100 MB.
- How: Java 25 no longer contains `ct.sym` (only used by the Java compiler, which the runtime doesn't include); the jars of the launcher's components are packed with xz instead of being compressed class by class; APKs no longer carry a Java runtime or a graphics driver that can't work on their CPU (Java 25 has no 32-bit x86 build, and the Panfrost driver is for ARM Mali GPUs only); and only the 9 languages the launcher is translated into are kept from the libraries.

**Everything else:**
- Renderers whose driver isn't included for your device's CPU are no longer offered (on x86 devices, Freedreno, Panfrost and VirGL were listed but could only fail).
- An interrupted first start (app closed, storage full) no longer leaves a half-unpacked component behind, and an error while unpacking no longer crashes the launcher.
- **Security:** modpacks, world downloads and Java runtimes can no longer write files outside their target folder ("Zip Slip" path traversal).
- Fixed symbolic links inside Java runtimes being created the wrong way round.
- Fixed the notice and sponsor checks getting stuck (never retrying) after a check was skipped or failed.
- Fixed importing worlds when the ZIP contains several `level.dat` files or the world is at the root of the ZIP.
- Modpack downloads now try every mirror before failing.
- Per-architecture APKs no longer include Java runtime files for other CPU types; a runtime that is missing for your CPU is skipped instead of breaking the unpacking step.
- Fixed a possible crash in the update downloader.
- Accounts are excluded from Android cloud backups.
- Update checks, notices and links now point to the Gurkha Launcher repository.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the checksums of all APKs.
